look_here_first: FIND THE ROSETTE and a WHOLE LEAF. Cedar sage is a taprooted PERENNIAL with low rosette and stem leaves, usually on long petioles; leaves can be simple (one terminal leaflet) or pinnately 3-foliolate with two smaller lateral leaflets. Many basal blades rounded/heart-shaped, unlike scarlet sage's simple deltoid leaves up an upright stem or big red sage's broad, thick, smooth rosette. Then inspect red tubular flowers and shaded cedar-juniper habitat.
project_tracker_diagnostic: taprooted rosetted perennial; basal plus cauline leaves; leaves rounded/cordate to lyrate-pinnatifid; red long-exserted corolla; late-season cleistogamous flowers can occur; shade/cedar-duff association

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Wildflower Center printable Hays County native list / local Hays flora sources. Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly includes Salvia roemeriana. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County detailed treatment.

best_field_traits: very long petioles; some leaves can appear nearly peltate in field view
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey highlights the red tubular flower and the unusually long petioles, describing the leaves as nearly peltate in appearance. This is a useful field cue when the basal rosette is visible.
morphology_keys.habit: Taprooted rosetted woodland perennial, one to several ascending flower stems from basal crown; often under Ashe juniper in leafy duff/limestone shade.
morphology_keys.leaves: UT Austin: opposite, 1–3 foliolate, often seemingly a single broad terminal leaflet with cordate base or two smaller lateral leaflets; long petioles, terminal blade to about 50 × 55 mm, soft/velveteen hair. Some leaves appear nearly peltate but petiole actually attaches at leaf base.
morphology_keys.flowering_nodes: Paired three-flowered cymes at successive flowering nodes; red/crimson tubular corollas and persistent calyx, calyx green with purple ridges/tips.
morphology_keys.flower_measurement: UT Austin corolla tube/throat to about 17 mm plus lips ~11.5 mm (complex overlapping measures); do NOT present as a 4-cm Big Red sage flower.
morphology_keys.diagnostic_calyx: Calyx roughly 11 mm tube length, purplish veined and long-pointed at upper tip; measure with scale if teaching fine IDs.
morphology_keys.habit_vs_big_red: Both rosetted, but Big Red sage's thick, dark-green smooth basal leaves to 12 cm and pink-red 4 cm corollas on 1.5 m stalks are usually much larger and often moist ravine/seep-associated.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Salvia coccinea: Both can be red. Cedar sage is rosetted and usually low in shaded juniper habitat; S. coccinea is taller with broad deltoid/ovate leaves along the stem.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.look_here_first: Cedar sage is NOT just 'small scarlet sage'. Check basal ROSETTE and sometimes COMPOUND leaves (1–3 leaflets) plus long petioles; flowering stem and shade support.

steps.trait: Cedar sage a perennial basal rosette with long-petioled leaves; scarlet sage has many simple stem leaves, big red also rosetted but robust.
Some cedar leaves have up to three leaflets; terminal leaflet cordate or roundish; photo both lamina and petiole.
Two opposite cymes usually with three flowers each; do not confuse an opposite cymose verticil with whole inflorescence.
Crimson two-lipped tube; green-purple ribbed long-tipped calyx; do not rely on crimson color alone.
Shade/cedar duff is a strong supporting cue, not definitive compared with flower/leaf morphology.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: CEDAR = cedar shade, ROSETTE, and a leaf that can show LITTLE SIDE LEAFLETS.
